clue.text: First man (not third) in contest, hard to criticise

indicators.note: the shortened first man sits inside the word for a contest, so 'in' signals the container

parts.note: a bout is a contest, as in boxing

indicators.note: the third letter of the first man's name is dropped, so this phrase marks a deletion

parts.note: Adam is the first man in Genesis
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Adam, demoted from third place in some competition, finds it hard to take criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not third)' drops the third letter of the first man's name, and the parentheses hide that it is an instruction; 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To badmouth someone is to speak ill of them, a slangy synonym for criticising.

clue.text: Central features of basic breakfast incorporating grilled toast

indicators.note: the middle letter of each of the next four words is taken, as 'central' marks their centres

explanation.surface: The essential parts of a simple breakfast include some grilled toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incorporating' looks like a container signal but is just one of the four words whose middle letter is picked: S, K, O, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Skol is a Scandinavian drinking salutation, so it serves as a toast when glasses are raised.

clue.text: Try to get up the pole, climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word reads upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: 'up the pole' is British slang for mad, the same as bats

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to shin up a pole, climbing hand over hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the pole' reads as a place to climb but is British slang for crazy, i.e. BATS; 'climbing' turns that into STAB. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means making an attempt, so stab is a noun for a try.

clue.text: Keeping in the shade?

parts.note: suggests staying out of the sun, but 'shade' means a hue: fabric whose dye holds its colour through washing

explanation.definitionFit: Dyed cloth that does not run or fade keeps its original hue, which is exactly what this term describes.

clue.text: Eggs around most of enclosure for birds

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around

indicators.note: the last letter of the bird enclosure is cut off, leaving most of the word

parts.note: an aviary is a large cage or enclosure for birds

explanation.surface: Eggs lie scattered about most of a birdhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the final Y from AVIARY; C (circa) goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is the salted roe of sturgeon, i.e. fish eggs served as a delicacy.

clue.text: Enjoy snaring king in conflict, obtaining easy victory

indicators.note: the whole inner unit sits inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: snaring means catching and holding, so the verb for enjoy surrounds the king's letter

parts.note: to love something is to enjoy it
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone relishes trapping a king in battle and wins without breaking a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snaring' puts the king's letter just after the first letter, giving LKOVE, before 'in' places the lot inside the conflict word; 'obtaining' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is a win gained with little or no opposition, like a contest where the rival fails to show.

clue.text: Express anger about cold chamber

parts.note: to vent feelings is to express them

indicators.note: the word for anger goes round the letter for cold

parts.note: to rile someone is to anger them
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone vents their fury over a chilly room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express anger' reads as one phrase but splits in two: a verb for letting feelings out, then a verb for annoying wrapped 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the lower chambers of the heart, also a cavity in the brain.

clue.text: Trapdoor's opening, right in middle of trick, showing part of trunk

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the letter for right is placed in the centre of the word for a trick

parts.note: a hoax is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: A magician's trapdoor opens mid-trick to reveal part of a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a box in a conjuring act, but it is the body's torso; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest, the part of the torso between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: Ocean covering large area mentioned in shipping forecast

indicators.note: the word for ocean wraps around the letter for large

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: An ocean covering a vast area gets a mention in the radio shipping report.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shipping Forecast is a BBC radio bulletin dividing the seas around Britain into named areas, Malin being one off northwest Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Malin is one of the named sea regions read out in the BBC maritime weather bulletin.

clue.text: Scoff at gathering of Olympians?

parts.note: 'scoff' looks like a verb meaning mock, but it is British slang for food: what was eaten when the gods of Olympus met

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the food of the gods, eaten on Mount Olympus to keep them immortal.

clue.text: Member of tribe with sorrow, on reflection, about cultivation of earth? He's no farmer

parts.note: a Hun is a member of the nomadic tribe led by Attila

indicators.note: the reversed sorrow word goes round the rearranged earth
reflected in a mirror, the word reads backwards

parts.note: regret is sorrow over something done

indicators.note: cultivating earth turns it over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns the sorrow word into TERGER; 'cultivation of' rearranges the soil word into ATHER, which 'about' places inside as TERG-ATHER-ER. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person lives by hunting animals and foraging wild food rather than growing crops.

clue.text: Insubstantial number apprehending notice over counter

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing, so the number holds the next two pieces inside

parts.note: three is a number

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the notice comes before the counter

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A small number of officers arrest someone for posting a notice above a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means above, so the notice comes before the counter; the pair splits the number word after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn thin, and figuratively a threadbare argument is flimsy and weak.

clue.text: Unconventional man walked round Spain with animal

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the word for walked goes round the letter for Spain

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to walk
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
an ox is an animal; 'with' adds it on

explanation.surface: An eccentric fellow wandered around Spain accompanied by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E inside TROD to give TEROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodox views depart from accepted belief, the opposite of orthodox.

clue.text: Greek poet? Not me — outstanding Roman poet

indicators.note: 'Not me' tells us to take the letters of me out of the Greek poet

parts.note: Homer is the Greek poet of the Iliad and Odyssey
the letters of me are removed
ace means excellent or outstanding

explanation.surface: A poet disowns the Greek label: no, he is a celebrated Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not me' strips ME from HOMER, leaving HOR, then ACE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a leading lyric poet of Augustan Rome, author of the Odes.

clue.text: Series from Jonathan Dimbleby's imminent

indicators.note: a run of consecutive letters is taken from the broadcaster's name

explanation.surface: A new television series from the broadcaster Jonathan Dimbleby is coming soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series' suggests a TV programme, but it is a string of letters running across 'jonATHAN Dimbleby's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by in time, about to happen, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Rock idol to me appears in fantastic form

indicators.note: a fantastic form is a wildly altered shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock idol tells a fan he appears to them in an imaginary guise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock idol' reads as a music star, but 'Rock' is the definition and 'idol to me' the fodder; 'appears in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolomite is a sedimentary rock made of calcium magnesium carbonate, giving its name to the Italian mountains.

clue.text: Soldiers very entertained by one narrating old, unlikely yarn

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in as a guest, so the narrator holds the soldiers and very

parts.note: a teller is someone who tells a story
RA stands for Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British army
stale means old and no longer fresh

explanation.surface: A storyteller regales soldiers with a hoary, implausible tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts the gunners and V just after the narrator's first letter, giving the first word of the phrase; RA is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story of the kind once told by returning voyagers, exaggerated and hard to believe.

clue.text: One after time at head of government becoming emperor

indicators.note: the time letter sits at the top of the government word in this down entry
the word for one comes after the rest

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Someone takes over at the top of government, after a period, and is crowned emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman ruler of the second century, under whom the empire reached its widest extent.

clue.text: Bizarre cult's enshrining love for tree

indicators.note: to enshrine is to hold within, so the rearranged letters surround the letter for love
bizarre means strange or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A strange sect worships its sacred love for a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CULTS are rearranged ('Bizarre') round O ('enshrining'), the 's supplying its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The locust is a leguminous tree, such as the carob or the North American honey locust.

clue.text: Uncivilised restrictions I start to challenge

the second bar, as the plural asks for more than one

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'restrictions' supplies two BARs; then I and C, the first letter of 'challenge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric behaviour is savage and crude, lacking the manners of civilisation.

clue.text: Judge with wig

clue.text: Material, obtained from excavation, to be put back

clue.text: Good new nosh

explanation.definitionFit: Neat is informal praise meaning excellent, as in 'that's a neat idea'.

clue.text: Room in good nick after last of dampness is eradicated

indicators.note: eradicated means wiped out, so the letter is removed from the word for nick

parts.note: to nick someone is British slang for to arrest them

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

clue.text: Navigational instruments still to be found aboard steamer

indicators.note: being aboard a ship means being inside it, so the steamer's letters surround the word

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
extant means still in existence

explanation.surface: Navigation tools are still kept on board a steamship.
